I chose option C: leave `validate.yml` on `setup-runtime@stable` and make no code change. Options A and B each need a 40-hex commit SHA that I could not find anywhere available to this run.

DECISIONS:
Q1: C

RATIONALE:
Q1: Options A and B both need the 40-hex SHA of a `main` commit, and I could not locate one. GITHUB FACTS only say that PR #7538 merged into `main` at 2026-10-17T08:42:20Z, without the merge commit SHA. The checkout has no git history, and no file (changelog fragment, agents fragment or the test) records a SHA for #7538. The data-provision guard therefore rules out A and B, and the implementer cannot derive the SHA either, because its sandbox has no commit history. Option C is safe: `.github/actions/setup-runtime/action.yml:54` already pins `install-codex@91b30f6fba400686c5dded34423f88f1ea10e163`, so validate runs normally on `@stable`, and the issue itself says this gap does not block. `tests/test_workflow_support_ref_follows_pin.py:202` keeps the single allow-list entry `("validate.yml", "setup-runtime@stable")`, so no other moving ref can slip in.

SETUP REQUIRED (only when a decision relies on a placeholder):
- PR_7538_MERGE_SHA (resource: a commit SHA a person looks up, not a secret): a person reads the merge commit of PR #7538 with `gh pr view 7538 --json mergeCommit -q .mergeCommit.oid`, or takes a later `main` commit whose `.github/actions/setup-runtime/action.yml` carries the pinned `install-codex`. With that SHA they open a follow-up that does two things:
  - changes `.github/workflows/validate.yml:406` to `setup-runtime@<sha>`;
  - removes the allow-list entry at `tests/test_workflow_support_ref_follows_pin.py:202`.
  Until then, `validate.yml` keeps `setup-runtime@stable` and the test keeps allowing exactly that one reference. If the SHA is pasted into a reply to this issue, re-planning with option A or B can proceed with no other change.
